question: Expression sqrt{(1 + sintheta)/(1 - sintheta)} is equal to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sinθ)

⇒ (1 + sinθ)/(1 − sinθ) = (1 + sinθ)² / (1 − sin²θ)

⇒ denominator = cos²θ

⇒ whole expression = √[(1 + sinθ)² / cos²θ]

⇒ = (1 + sinθ)/cosθ = sectheta + tantheta 

**∴ Answer = sectheta + tantheta **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

√[(1 + sinθ)/(1 − sinθ)]

**Formula used:**

1 − sin²θ = cos²θ

 
 A B C cosθ sinθ 

Using identity: 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ

**Calculation:**

⇒ √[(1 + sinθ)/(1 − sinθ)]

⇒ Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sinθ)

⇒ = √[(1 + sinθ)² / (1 − sin²θ)]

⇒ = √[(1 + sinθ)² / cos²θ]

⇒ = (1 + sinθ)/cosθ = sectheta + tantheta 

**∴ The correct answer is sectheta + tantheta **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identity

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

Transformation Trick

Multiply by conjugate to simplify expressions.

Equivalent Forms

(1 + sinθ)/cosθ = secθ + tanθ

Common Identity

√[(1 + sinθ)/(1 − sinθ)] = secθ + tanθ
